title: Section check: Trade, power and everyday lives
intro: 6 questions about Lessons 4–6. Take your time. You can look back at the lessons and try again as often as you like.

options.text: Many buyers try to buy the same spice.
options.feedback: Not quite. When many buyers can compete, no one has a monopoly. Look back at Lesson 4.

options.text: One buyer shuts all the others out.
options.feedback: Yes. The VOC wanted to be the only buyer of Banda's nutmeg, so no one else could compete.
Not quite. Swapping goods is a kind of trade. A monopoly is when one group shuts other buyers or sellers out. Look back at Lesson 4.

questions.question: The painting of Banda Neira cannot tell the whole story. Why not?

options.text: It was made for the VOC, much later
options.feedback: Yes. The VOC paid for it more than 40 years after 1621. It shows the company's view, not what Bandanese people lived through.

options.text: It was painted before nutmeg grew there
options.feedback: Not quite. Nutmeg grew on Banda for hundreds of years before the painting. It shows rows of nutmeg trees. Look back at Lesson 4.

options.text: A painting can never be used as evidence
options.feedback: Not quite. The painting is useful evidence. It shows how the company chose to show Banda. It just cannot tell the whole story. Look back at Lesson 4.

questions.question: Rubber went from a tree to a buyer far away. Which work did workers do on the way?

options.text: Buying shares in a rubber company
options.feedback: Not quite. An investor bought shares, hoping to get more money back. Look back at Lesson 5.

options.text: Choosing photos for a souvenir book
options.feedback: Not quite. The book's makers chose the photos. Workers tapped trees and collected and carried the rubber. Look back at Lesson 5.
Yes. Workers tapped each tree and collected the latex. Others made it into sheets and took it to ships.

stimulus.title: A made-up postcard from a made-up tea estate
stimulus.body: This is a made-up example. A postcard from 1925 shows a tea estate on the made-up hill of Tavin. Rows of tea bushes cover the hill. Two workers pick leaves into baskets. A shop sold the postcard to visitors.

questions.question: Which source could tell you what these workers were paid?

options.text: A bigger copy of the same postcard
options.feedback: Not quite. A bigger copy shows the same scene. A picture cannot show pay. Look back at Lesson 5.

options.text: A pay record from the estate
options.feedback: Yes. Pay is written in records, or told by the workers. A postcard shows only what its makers chose.

options.text: The number of baskets in the picture
options.feedback: Not quite. The baskets show the work, not the pay. Look back at Lesson 5.

questions.question: In 1903, Kartini and her sister were offered a scholarship. What happened next?

options.text: The sisters did not use the money.
options.feedback: Yes. A decision shows what officials agreed to. It does not show what happened next. The sisters did not use the money.

options.text: Kartini used it to study in Batavia.
options.feedback: Not quite. The money was offered for study in Batavia. But the sisters did not use it. Look back at Lesson 6.

options.text: Kartini used it to open her school.
options.feedback: Not quite. The school was a hope in her 1901 letter. The scholarship was a different thing, and it was not used. Look back at Lesson 6.

questions.question: You read Kartini's 1901 letter in an English book from 1921. Which question is good to ask about it?

options.text: Why did Kartini write it in English?
options.feedback: Not quite. Kartini wrote mostly in Dutch. The English words are a translation. Look back at Lesson 6.
Not quite. The letter is from 1901, and it tells us a hope. The decision is a different source. Look back at Lesson 6.

options.text: Who chose and translated the letters?
options.feedback: Yes. An editor chose which letters to print, and the book has only some of them. A translator made choices too.

results.high: Well done. You asked who made each source, and whose story it leaves out.
results.middle: Good work. You got many questions right. Look back at the lessons for the ones you missed, and try again if you like.
results.low: Thank you for trying. Look back at Lessons 4–6, then try again. You can take as long as you need.
